lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.Grover:QuantumComputation.Specs.groverParallelMarkingOracle
lean.plain: Parallel marking oracle in the challenge
lean.annotation: A slot can be disabled without knowing any unmarked address. Since $X|+\rangle=|+\rangle$, the oracle acts as the identity on that slot whenever its target qubit is prepared in $|+\rangle$. This also works when its address is entangled with the rest of the workspace.

lean.name: QuantumComputationDiscoveries.Algorithms.GroverFindAny:QuantumComputation.Specs.groverParallelMarkingOracle
lean.annotation: With the target qubits in $|-\rangle$, the product oracle multiplies an address tuple by $(-1)^{\sum_j[x_j\in S]}$. Two marked positions give two factors of $-1$ and a net sign of $+1$. One round gives this parity phase, which suffices for Find-Any.

lean.name: ResourceCounting.expectedCost
lean.annotation: If one query is followed by a second on an outcome of probability $1/4$, the expected cost is $1+1/4$ rounds. In `expectedCost`, the state passed to the second query already has trace $1/4$, so the `.qAssign` case multiplies its unit cost by $1/4$.

lean.name: ResourceCounting.whileRecCost_succ
lean.plain: Expected cost of a guarded loop
lean.annotation: For a loop with one query per iteration, let $T$ be the number of iterations. The guard reaches query $r+1$ with probability $\Pr(T>r)$. The first $L$ unrollings therefore cost $\sum_{r=0}^{L-1}\Pr(T>r)$ in expectation. Taking the supremum counts the whole loop, including a query that succeeds.

lean.name: ResourceCounting.CostModel.ofEmbeddedOracle
lean.plain: Charging one round per embedded oracle
lean.annotation: An embedded marking oracle is a real permutation matrix. To apply a free real unitary $U$ without coinciding with that matrix, the circuit uses the globally phased unitary $iU$ in `phaseTag`. Both give the same evolution of density matrices, and `ofEmbeddedOracle` assigns the phased matrix cost zero.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.Grover:QuantumComputation.Specs.groverParallelMarkingOracle
lean.plain: Parallel marking oracle in the challenge
lean.annotation: The product applies $O_S$ to each disjoint query register, even when the registers share an entangled state. Between rounds, Find-Any reflects about the uniform state of all $mn$ address qubits. That joint diffusion amplifies the odd-parity part of the state.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.Grover:QuantumComputation.Specs.groverParallelMarkingOracle
lean.plain: Parallel marking oracle in the challenge
lean.annotation: An oracle call acts within its $m$ chosen query registers. Other unitaries can act across the shared workspace. In Find-Any, for example, the diffusion uses all $mn$ address qubits together, while the same $m$ target qubits are reused for the weak checks and final membership readout.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.Grover:QuantumComputation.Specs.groverParallelMarkingOracle
lean.plain: Parallel marking oracle in the challenge
lean.annotation: For a single slot the basis index is $2x+b$, where $b$ is the low-order target bit. At $n=3$, marking address $5$ exchanges the basis indices $10$ and $11$. The parallel oracle embeds this permutation into every block starting at wire $i(n+1)$.

statements.markdown: where $b$ is a single-qubit target bit and $x$ is the $n$-qubit index
